clue.text: Excellent form of transport, and well ventilated

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, written with the letter I standing in for the one
RY is the standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A traveller praises a vehicle that is both superb and pleasantly breezy inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 for excellent is a crossword staple, read as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A room that is airy has plenty of fresh breeze moving through it, the plain synonym sense.

clue.text: Weapon appears in a catalogue, causing needless panic

definitions.note: the answer as an adjective, describing something that spreads alarm

indicators.note: the weapon shows up inside the other phrase, placed within it

blocks.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearm
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A gun shows up in a mail-order brochure and frightens people unnecessarily.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist warning exaggerates danger, frightening people more than the facts justify.

clue.text: In America, the permanent way to coerce

blocks.note: first meaning: the American name for a railway track
second meaning: force someone into something

explanation.surface: An American insists on the fixed route to bully people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The permanent way' is the British railway term for the track and its bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans say this for a railway line, and also use it as a verb meaning to pressure someone into acting.

clue.text: Fall in dark beside climbing shrub

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first is placed inside the second

blocks.note: dark as in without light
by means next to
to fall from grace is to sin, to go wrong

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles in the dark next to a bush they are trying to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' looks like a tumble or autumn, but here it is the moral sense: to fall is to sin, to go astray.
explanation.definitionFit: The bramble is a thorny scrambling plant that sprawls and climbs over hedges, bearing dark fruit.

clue.text: Highly inebriated bishop leaves for game

indicators.note: the bishop departs, so his abbreviation is taken out of the word

blocks.note: slang for very drunk
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A drunken bishop walks out to go and play a game.
explanation.definitionFit: This numbers game, like bingo, has players marking cards as numbers are drawn at random.

clue.text: Meeting in the station area

blocks.note: first meaning: a coming together, a gathering
second meaning: the large open hall of a railway terminus

explanation.surface: A rendezvous arranged in part of a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a crowd or confluence, and also the open hall at a railway terminal or airport.

clue.text: Single condition from composer and poet holding up function

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Johann Sebastian, the German composer
a function is a role or job
Thomas Hood, the English poet

explanation.surface: Being unmarried, a musician and a writer prop up a social event.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the poet sits under the turned function and so holds it up. Thomas Hood was a Victorian comic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of an unmarried man is literally a condition of being single.

clue.text: A justification of sanity

blocks.note: first meaning: a ground or cause for doing something
second meaning: a sound mind, as in losing one's mind

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a cause or explanation for an action and the faculty of rational thought.

clue.text: Acquiescent types originally serving in Asian republic

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the opening letter is used
one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: the country at the south of the Arabian peninsula
the opening letter of serving

explanation.surface: Compliant people who first served in an Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadies who always agree with the boss are compliant, never saying no.

clue.text: A number backing the alliance

indicators.note: going backwards means the number is written from its end to its start

blocks.note: taken as written
a number spelt out in letters

explanation.surface: Some figure lends its support to a coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany, Italy and Japan were known as the Axis powers in the Second World War, a famous military pact.

clue.text: Songsters from single church visiting countries out East

indicators.note: the compass point named next is put outside, dropped from the word
a visitor goes inside someone else's place, so these letters sit within the other word

blocks.note: nations, as in sovereign states
the compass abbreviation
one means a single unit
the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Choristers from a lone church tour foreign lands in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing E from STATES leaves STATS, and ONE plus CH go into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: These small birds are songbirds, named for a call that sounds like two pebbles clicked together.

clue.text: Dog bounds over pass with rest

blocks.note: a border marks the bounds of a place
a col is a mountain pass
to lie is to rest

explanation.surface: A dog leaps across a mountain pass and then takes a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounds' looks like a verb for the dog leaping, but it is a noun meaning limits.
explanation.definitionFit: This sheepdog breed, from the region between England and Scotland, is a well-known working dog.

clue.text: Brandy and game tucked into by old Venetian traveller

indicators.note: something tucked into a pair is pushed into the gap between them

blocks.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape pressings
the sport played on horseback with mallets
the usual abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An elderly man from Venice is served spirits and plays a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' seems to belong with the traveller, but it is wordplay; marc is a brandy made from grape skins left after pressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirteenth-century merchant journeyed from Venice to the court of Kublai Khan and wrote of his travels.

clue.text: 'ow an 'orseman travelled to eat away?

indicators.note: the clue writes 'how' with its first letter missing, telling us to drop the aitch the same way

blocks.note: the rider is referred to as he
a horseman travels by riding

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks how a rider went about wearing something down.
explanation.walkthrough: How did a horseman travel? He rode; said with a dropped aitch, as the clue's own spelling demands, that is 'e rode.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind and water gradually wear rock down, which is the geological sense of gnawing at it.

clue.text: Surrogate stable-lad's limited accommodation

blocks.note: a stand-in substitutes for someone else
a groom looks after horses in a stable

explanation.surface: A substitute stable hand has only cramped lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's here is 'has', joining the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Space where people may stay upright but cannot sit is a restricted kind of room in a theatre or train.

clue.text: Get over treat

blocks.note: first meaning: get past an obstacle successfully
second meaning: hold talks, bargain

explanation.walkthrough: 'Treat' looks like a noun for a pleasure; it is the old verb, to treat with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: One can steer round a hazard or bend, and one can bargain with another party; the verb covers both.

clue.text: Organised group is imprisoned after appearing on trial for revolt

indicators.note: something imprisoned is shut inside, so these letters go within the group

blocks.note: to be up before the court is to be on trial
a ring is an organised gang, as in a smuggling ring
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gang members jailed after a court case for rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising against the authorities, an insurrection, is a revolt by a people.

clue.text: Is his display instrumental in attracting a mate?

definitions.text: Is his display instrumental in attracting a mate?

blocks.clueFragment: Is his display instrumental in attracting a mate?
blocks.note: surface reading: does a man's showing-off help him win a partner?
setter's reading: a creature whose courtship display is shaped like a musical instrument

explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrumental' means helpful in the surface but literally refers to a harp-shaped tail fanned out by an Australian bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The male of this Australian species spreads tail feathers resembling a lyre when courting females.

clue.text: Inclined to act rashly, threatening disturbing reports

blocks.note: first meaning: too quick to take drastic action
second meaning: a gunman ready to set off loud bangs at any moment

explanation.surface: A rash official threatens to leak alarming documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reports' looks like news but means gunshots; a gunman eager to fire threatens noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a shooter quick to pull the trigger, and by extension anyone reckless and hasty.

clue.text: Discharge account almost entirely

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: the abbreviation for account
quite means completely

explanation.surface: Settling an account very nearly in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A court discharges a defendant by declaring them not guilty and setting them free.

clue.text: Old servant in India - one who endures

blocks.note: first meaning: a porter or household servant under the Raj
second meaning: someone who puts up with something

explanation.surface: A former servant in colonial India puts up with a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Under British rule a domestic or palanquin-carrier had this title, and to bear something is to endure it.

clue.text: Firm embracing revolutionary beliefs

definitions.note: the answer is a single set of beliefs, a creed

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: the abbreviation for company
a red is a communist or revolutionary

explanation.surface: A company that takes on radical opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith or guiding principles, from the Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: Stall a conductor may demand?

blocks.note: first meaning: play for time, delay a decision
second meaning, read cryptically: an orchestra leader may ask the band to go faster

explanation.surface: A bus conductor asks for the fare at a market booth.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as TEMPO RISE: a quicker speed is what a conductor might call for.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to delay or evade commitment to gain time, much like stalling.

clue.text: Bishop, possibly, covering the Italian city

indicators.note: a covering goes over and around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a bishop is one of the pieces, or men, in chess
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: A cleric, perhaps, wrapping his cloak round the Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Italian city' reads as one phrase, but 'the Italian' gives IL and 'city' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lombard capital is a major northern Italian city, famous for fashion and its cathedral.

clue.text: About liberal reform, a Parisian is not to be trusted

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so the French word goes round the rearranged letters

blocks.note: taken as written
the French feminine word for a

explanation.surface: A French woman's views on liberal reform make her untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it means around: UNE wraps round the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undependable cannot be relied upon, so they ought not to be trusted.

clue.text: Sporty New Zealander, though not a flighty type

blocks.note: first meaning: a national player, as in the New Zealand rugby league team's nickname
second meaning: a bird that cannot fly

explanation.surface: An athletic man from New Zealand who is steady, not frivolous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' looks like fickle, but it means able to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The national bird of New Zealand is flightless, and its name is used for New Zealanders, especially sportspeople.

clue.text: Like a vile-sounding opera, of very little worth

blocks.note: first meaning: the title of the Brecht and Weill opera, whose name sounds cheap
second meaning: costing only a few old pence

explanation.surface: An opera that sounds dreadful and is hardly worth anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Vile in its old sense means cheap. The threepence was an old British coin worth three pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something priced at three old pennies was trivial and cheap, and the word came to mean worthless.

clue.text: Very old artist retiring without a shilling

indicators.note: going without something means the coin's abbreviation is left off
retiring means withdrawing, going back the way one came, so the name runs backwards

blocks.note: the French painter of ballet dancers
S is the abbreviation for shilling, the old British coin

explanation.surface: An elderly painter retires with no money left.
explanation.walkthrough: DEGAS loses its S, then reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged describes someone who has lived a long time, a plain synonym for elderly.
